answer: A harbor registry can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade. The stake is held in escrow and slashed if the identity cheats, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of stakes. The cost spreads like a ripple, growing linearly with each fake identity, while honest agents recover their stake after a clean record, so entry stays open but forgery backed by ferrous collateral becomes expensive at scale.
